summary.text: In one post-Homeric tradition recorded by Apollodorus, the son whom Odysseus left in Aetolia when he married the daughter of Thoas son of Andraemon and died there in old age — an ending wholly distinct from Homer's peaceful restoration on Ithaca and from the Telegonus tradition.

story.text: Apollodorus reports, as a variant ending to the Odyssey, that after the kinsfolk of the slain suitors accused Odysseus, Neoptolemus — king of the islands off Epirus and hoping to gain Cephallenia if Odysseus were removed — condemned him to exile. Odysseus went to Aetolia to Thoas son of Andraemon, married his daughter, and left a son Leontophonus by her before he died in old age.
